problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of 10 distribution centers across a regional network:

Center Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (71,161)  
Center Beta: Positioned at grid reference (5,30)  
Center Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (69,171)  
Center Delta: Positioned at grid reference (10,0)  
Center Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (65,101)  
Center Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (134,148)  
Center Eta: Positioned at grid reference (181,101)  
Center Theta: Positioned at grid reference (113,26)  
Center Iota: Positioned at grid reference (191,64)  
Center Kappa: Positioned at grid reference (90,72)

Transport distances between centers, measured in kilometers, are predetermined:
Alpha to Gamma: 10.2 km  
Alpha to Delta: 172.2 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 60.3 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 64.3 km  
Alpha to Eta: 125.3 km  
Alpha to Theta: 141.4 km  
Alpha to Iota: 154.3 km  
Alpha to Kappa: 91.0 km  
Beta to Gamma: 154.8 km  
Beta to Delta: 30.4 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 93.0 km  
Beta to Zeta: 174.8 km  
Beta to Eta: 189.8 km  
Beta to Theta: 108.1 km  
Beta to Iota: 189.1 km  
Beta to Kappa: 94.8 km  
Gamma to Delta: 180.9 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 70.1 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 68.9 km  
Gamma to Eta: 132.1 km  
Gamma to Theta: 151.5 km  
Gamma to Iota: 162.3 km  
Gamma to Kappa: 101.2 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 115.0 km  
Delta to Zeta: 193.1 km  
Delta to Eta: 198.6 km  
Delta to Theta: 106.2 km  
Delta to Iota: 192.0 km  
Delta to Kappa: 107.6 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 83.5 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 116.0 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 89.0 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 131.3 km  
Epsilon to Kappa: 38.3 km  
Zeta to Eta: 66.5 km  
Zeta to Theta: 123.8 km  
Zeta to Iota: 101.5 km  
Zeta to Kappa: 87.8 km  
Eta to Theta: 101.2 km  
Eta to Iota: 38.3 km  
Eta to Kappa: 95.5 km  
Theta to Iota: 86.8 km  
Theta to Kappa: 51.4 km  
Iota to Kappa: 101.3 km

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct transport link exists between Center Alpha and Center Beta.  
Furthermore, operational constraints mandate that exactly one of two specific corridors be utilized in the circuit: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal‑distance cyclical route that visits every distribution center precisely once and concludes at the origin center.
